subject: Change Order: Reserved GPU Pool Increase + SOW Task Reallocation
messages:
From: Timothy Jones <timothy.jones@nexahealth.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@nexahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Increase reserved GPU capacity + SOW task reallocation

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the throughput improvements look promising. We reviewed utilization for the pilot and need to request a formal change order to increase our reserved GPU pool from 10 to 24 GPUs for Q3 (effective May 1).

Two asks from our side:
- Add 14 reserved GPUs (same instance profile) and update the order form pricing accordingly.
- Reallocate the SOW task breakdown: move two integration tasks from Phase 2 to Phase 1 (integration of the inference cache & prefix routing). That affects delivery milestones and acceptance criteria in Exhibit B.

I've attached the current order form and a spreadsheet showing the proposed task moves for visibility. Can you share the redline/CO draft and an estimated timeline for legal review + sign-off? Procurement would like an invoice impact estimate (proration) and the change control authority.

Tim

--
Timothy Jones
Head of Platform Engineering, NexaHealth
T: 415-555-0184
--
Attachments: Existing_OrderForm_NEXA_v1.pdf, SOW_TaskList_v2.xlsx
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Timothy Jones <timothy.jones@nexahealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Increase reserved GPU capacity + SOW task reallocation

Tim — thanks for the clear ask and the task spreadsheet, appreciate the level of detail.

High-level plan from our side:
1) I will prepare a draft change order (CO) that: adds 14 GPUs to the reserved pool, updates line item pricing, and enumerates the SOW task reallocation in Exhibit B.
2) Karthik (cc'd) will coordinate legal redlines vs the MSA/Order Form and confirm any downstream compliance or DPA impacts.
3) Laura (cc'd) will provide the proration math & invoice timing once the effective date is confirmed (you proposed May 1).
4) We aim to have a redline-ready CO by EOD Wed (Apr 7) and target legal review + counter-sign by end of next week (Apr 14), subject to any material MSA changes.

Open questions for Nexa:
- Confirm the effective date you want (May 1?) and whether the GPUs need burst pool or strictly reserved (reserved preferred on our end).
- Any change to the data flows or retention requirements tied to Exhibit C we should be aware of (SOC2 scope).

I'll attach the draft CO and a short mutual action plan in the next email.

Thanks —
Priyom
Sr. Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

Office: +1 415-555-0112

On Mon, Apr 5, 2027 at 11:03 AM Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com> wrote:
> I'll attach the draft CO and a short mutual action plan in the next email.

Thanks — I reviewed Priyom's summary and the draft CO. A few legal / contract items to flag before finalizing:

1) MSA Exhibit A (Fees & Billing) — we need to ensure the order form reflects the correct SKU mapping to the Reserved GPU product and that the fee ladder in the Order Form aligns with the reserved pool pricing. If Nexa wants burst capability in addition to reserved, that's a separate SKU and affects the billing model.
2) SOW Exhibit B — when moving two integration tasks forward, we'll update acceptance criteria and milestone-linked payment triggers. Please confirm whether Nexa expects the same acceptance test matrix or if additional testcases are required for the cache/prefix features.
3) Data protection / DPA — moving tasks earlier may change when production telemetry flows. Priyom, please add a short note in the CO re: telemetry/retention if there are changes; procurement, please confirm.
4) Escalation / SLA exceptions — increasing reserved capacity is material. If Nexa requires a firm latency SLA for the new pool, that needs an SLA amendment and potentially a capacity commit.

I will insert legal redline callouts directly into CO-2027-04-05_ChangeOrder_draft.docx and return by Wednesday COB. Priyom, Laura — if procurement/finance confirm proration expectations, we can include a pro-forma invoice.

Karthik
Head of Commercial Contracts, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
--
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Timothy Jones <timothy.jones@nexahealth.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Apr 2027 13:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Increase reserved GPU capacity + SOW task reallocation

Tim, Priyom — looping in finance details.

Assuming an effective date of May 1, here's a quick proration approach we can use:
- Charge full rate for the new reserved GPUs from May 1 forward. For April partial month (if change order executed before May 1 with retroactive effect), we can pro-rate by daily usage.
- If Nexa prefers a credit model to offset the reallocated tasks (i.e., push some payment from Phase 2 earlier), we can model that as a line-item credit on the May invoice.

I'll prepare a pro-forma that shows: monthly run-rate before/after, one-time implementation fee delta (if any), and an estimated May invoice. Expect a PDF by EOD Wed.

Laura Bennett
Director, Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

Thanks — that timeline works for us. Confirming: effective date May 1, reserved only (no burst SKU), acceptance criteria remain the same besides the schedule shift. Procurement confirms no change to DPA at this time.

We reviewed the draft CO and added one small ask: include the implementation window (two-week ramp starting May 1) and a single rollback clause if production regressions happen during ramp. I attached our signed purchase intent form. Please send the redline back and the DocuSign envelope when ready — procurement would like an expedited signature path.

DocuSign envelope: https://www.docusign.com/txn/abc123-nexa-changeorder

Best,
Tim
